outcomes: Calculate a dot-product attention score for a tiny query and key
Explain why scaled dot products are passed through softmax
Trace how attention weights combine value vectors

glossary.definition: A learned vector representing the information a token is looking for.
A learned vector used to measure how relevant a token is to a query.

explanation.problem: A token needs to combine information from other tokens in its context.
explanation.plainLanguage: Imagine each token asking a question. Other tokens offer keys that can match that question. The matching scores decide how much information each token contributes. Attention makes this selection differentiable so a model can learn useful patterns from data.
explanation.mentalModel: Score relevance first, turn scores into weights, then use those weights to combine value vectors.
limitations: Attention weights are not a complete explanation of model behavior.
explanation.everydayAnalogy: A classroom discussion works like attention: each student asks a question, listens for classmates whose notes match it, then combines the useful notes. Queries are questions, keys are matching labels, values are the notes, and attention weights decide how much each note contributes.
explanation.mathMadeSimple: For q=[1,0], k1=[1,0], k2=[0,1], the dot scores are [1,0]. With key dimension 2, divide by √2 to get [0.7071,0]. Softmax gives about [0.6698,0.3302]. Combining v1=[2,0] and v2=[0,4] gives [1.3395,1.3210].
explanation.productionImpact: Incorrect masking can leak future tokens during training; unstable softmax can produce NaN values; wrong tensor shapes can crash inference. Attention also has quadratic sequence-length cost in its standard form, so long contexts increase memory, latency and serving cost.

useCase.scenario: A decoder model processes a sentence and uses earlier tokens to build the next token representation.
constraints: Future tokens must be masked in causal decoding.
useCase.successMetric: Numerical output matches the deterministic reference fixture.

dataFlow.purpose: Create query, key and value representations

trustBoundaries: Model weights and input data are treated as separate assets.
failurePaths: Incorrect tensor dimensions cause a matrix multiplication failure.

steps.label: Project vectors
steps.explanation: Create Q, K and V from the input.
steps.expectedState: Q, K and V have matching token dimensions.

steps.label: Calculate weights
steps.expectedState: Weights sum to one for each unmasked query.

accessibility: Every step has a text explanation.
The visual supports keyboard step navigation.

animation.objective: Trace the same two-key attention fixture through scoring, normalization and weighted value aggregation.

stages.title: Compare query and keys
stages.narration: Each key is compared with the query using a dot product. The first key aligns perfectly; the second does not.
stages.visualState: Two score bars show key 1 higher than key 2

stages.title: Normalize scores
stages.narration: Softmax converts scores into positive weights that add up to one.
stages.transformation: Exponentiate after max subtraction, then divide by the sum
stages.visualState: A probability bar allocates 66.98% to value 1 and 33.02% to value 2

stages.title: Combine value vectors
stages.narration: Each value is multiplied by its attention weight, then the weighted vectors are added.
stages.visualState: Two weighted vector contributions merge into one context vector

controls.name: temperature
controls.effect: Lower values sharpen the weight distribution; higher values make it more uniform. This is an educational control over score sharpness.

controls.name: keyAlignment
controls.effect: Reduce the first key alignment to shift attention away from value 1 and observe the output vector change.

animation.accessibilitySummary: Every animation frame has a matching text narration, explicit input and output values, and keyboard-accessible previous and next controls. Reduced-motion mode must retain the same numerical step sequence without animated movement.

workedExample.problem: Combine two value vectors using a query and two keys.

steps.reasoning: Compare the query with each key.

implementations.expectedResult: Stable scaled attention weights and context vector match the deterministic fixture.

failures.name: Shape mismatch
failures.symptom: Matrix multiplication raises a dimension error.
failures.rootCause: Query and key dimensions do not align.
failures.recovery: Assert the final dimension before multiplication.

failures.name: Unstable softmax
failures.recovery: Subtract the maximum score before exponentiation.
failures.regressionTest: Test large positive and negative scores.

failures.name: Causal leakage
failures.symptom: A decoder position can use a future token.
failures.rootCause: The causal mask is missing or inverted.
failures.recovery: Apply the upper-triangular mask before softmax.

practice.guided: Calculate the attention output for two tokens by hand.
practice.independent: Implement scaled dot-product attention with a causal mask.
practice.realWorld: Trace attention for a short next-token prediction request.
practice.expertExtension: Compare attention memory and compute cost as sequence length grows.

rubric.criterion: Explain query, key and value roles
